thing.name: ownship
thing.description: The simulated vehicle the sampling platform rides on. Its own datastreams carry its motion, and a series of them is its track.

platform.name: sampling platform A
platform.description: A simulated sampling platform. A coordinate and a sampler.

tunables.label: drift threshold
tunables.description: How far a measured sound speed may sit from the forecast before the sample counts as breaching. Lower it and the loop turns sooner.

tunables.label: persistence
tunables.description: Consecutive breaching samples before a divergence is raised. Never one: a single spike is not drift.

tunables.label: minimum interval
tunables.description: No two runs closer together than this. A divergence inside it is declined by policy, and the decline is published.

tunables.label: cadence floor
tunables.description: The interval after which a run is warranted on schedule alone. Whether it is then requested at once or held is decided against the cost the model runner published, never here.

tunables.label: sampling cadence
tunables.description: How often the instruments sample the ocean. The loop’s master dial: shorten it and residuals, store growth and the monitor’s streak all quicken. It is also how long a heard position stays fresh, so shortening it below the platform’s reporting interval makes the sensors go quiet for want of a current position — they say so, and the dial below is the other half of the pair.

tunables.label: usable doubt
tunables.description: The doubt above which the planner calls a region unusable. Raise it and fewer regions are worth visiting; the planner still recommends and commands nothing.

tunables.label: ownship reporting
tunables.description: How often the platform reports where it is. The sensors sample where it last said it was and treat a position older than their own cadence as no position at all, so this is the dial that keeps them supplied when their cadence is shortened.

events.label: request a forecast run
events.description: Ask the scheduler to consider a run now. It answers under the policy it applies to a divergence, so it may decline inside the minimum interval or while a run is outstanding — and either way the decision is published.

events.label: author an advisory
events.description: Ask the shore source to author the next advisory in its sequence now rather than at its cadence. Prompted or not, it is the same deterministic next one.

events.label: publish a now-cast
events.description: Ask the ocean generator to author and publish its next now-cast now rather than at its cadence. It supersedes the one before it — there is one now-cast at a time — and lands in the coverage store and on the map. It does not change what the sensors read: they sample the world through their own port, continuously.

events.label: recompute the plan
events.description: Ask the planner to recompute now rather than at its replan interval. With no uncertainty field to work from it says so in its heartbeat and publishes no hollow plan. It recommends either way; nothing here turns a recommendation into an order.

events.label: stage a package
events.description: Ask the packager to stage a window now over the release it last heard. It answers under the rules it already has: declined at its staging bound, and declined where the interval holds no measurements, because a bundle nobody can score is not staged.

events.label: publish a faulty sample
events.description: Ask the instruments to publish one deliberately malformed observation. The ingestion seam refuses it against the committed master and names the fault; the sensors count what they were asked to produce and say so.

events.label: report an impossible depth
events.description: Ask the platform to report one depth beyond the maximum it declares it can reach. The ingestion seam flags it against the platform’s own limits and names the bound; the platform counts what it was asked to produce and says so.

events.label: sample now
events.description: Ask the instruments to take one sample now rather than at their cadence. It is the ordinary sampling path under the ordinary declared noise; only the timing is asked for. With no fresh ownship position there is nothing to sample at, and the instruments say so rather than inventing a place to have been.

events.label: report position now
events.description: Ask the platform to report where it is now rather than at its reporting interval. The other half of the sample prompt: instruments quiet for want of a fresh position are waiting on exactly this message. An observation's id is a function of its tick, so a prompt at a tick already reported is the same measurement and the store treats it as the redelivery it is.

events.label: announce holdings
events.description: Ask the store to announce its current era pointers again. Nothing is published and nothing changes — the announcement names holdings that already exist, over the same bytes and the same digests. With none published the store says so rather than announcing an absence.

events.label: publish the skill statement
events.description: Ask telemetry to publish its forecast-skill statement now rather than at its cadence. It says what a statement on cadence says, including that there are too few samples to score.

events.label: publish residual statistics
events.description: Ask telemetry to publish its residual statistics now rather than at its cadence. With nothing folded it publishes the named absence it would publish anyway, never a zero.
